title: Compact PR annotator workflow & quick-review TODO
content:
Purpose: compact, reusable checklist and lightweight annotator pattern I can paste into PR comments. Fast mental model for reviewers and a short-term backlog of follow-ups for larger refactors. Keep as a single-note brain-dump — will extract into a lint bot template when stabilized.

Top-level goals (why):
- keep PR review time < 20m for small changes (<= 40 LOC)
- capture follow-ups for cross-cutting refactors instead of blocking merges
- ensure safety-critical changes have clear test signal and rollback plan

Quick-review checklist (paste into PR comment):
- Summary: 1–2 lines describing change and user-visible impact.
- Size classification: tiny / small / medium / large (> 500LOC avoid fast-track).
- Tests: unit / integration / e2e added? list filenames. If none, explain why.
- Perf/regression risk: none / minor / major. Baseline numbers (before -> after) if major.
- DB/migration: no / safe / destructive. Migration plan link if applicable.
- Secrets/config changes: list cfg keys and fallback behavior.
- Rollback plan: quick revert steps + smoke test to validate.
- Owner & contact: @handle + days available for rollback.

Annotator workflow (how I annotate):
1) Read PR title + first two commits. If unclear, ask for 1-line intent.
2) Skim diff for hotpaths + call sites (search for `apply_batch`, `kv_cache`). Mark any unfamiliar modules.
3) Run quick local sanity: `make dev-up` + minimal repro (commands below).
4) Leave structured comment using Quick-review checklist above.
5) Add inline comments where behavior is subtle or preconditions assumed. Use `nit:` for style; `blocking:` for things that must be fixed.
6) If > 2 blocking comments, suggest splitting PR and list split candidates.
7) If performance sensitive, request a perf-run or benchmark harness PR (see follow-ups).

Local repro commands (cheats):
- start minimal server: `docker-compose -f docker/dev-compose.yml up --build -d redis kvstore`
- run unit subset: `pytest tests/unit/test_kv_cache.py::TestKVCache::test_prefix_eviction -q`
- quick load test: `wrk -t2 -c50 -d10s http://localhost:8080/v1/generate?model=redwood-small`
- trace capture: `TRACE=1 go run ./cmd/infer --sample`

Refactor idea bank (short notes, non-blocking):
- split `kv_cache` into `kv_cache/core` + `kv_cache/policy` to isolate eviction heuristics. Add migration shim for a single release.
- extract `sequence_length_stats` collector into a separate thread to reduce lock contention in hot loops.
- replace some `sync.Mutex` in `batcher` with sharded atomics for counter-only state. Measure delta.

Follow-ups (to file as issues or future PRs):
- PERF-PL-1: bench harness for small models in CI (target: detect 10% regression). Link: linear above.
- CLEANUP-3: consolidate error types in `api/errors.go` (too many wrappers, hard to assert in tests).
- OBS-9: per-request token breakdown in traces (tokenize stage -> model stage -> writeback).

Risk matrix for this change (quick):
- correctness: low/medium/high (describe reason)
- perf: low/medium/high (hotpath? kernel change?)
- infra: low/medium/high (requires infra rollout?)
- user-impact: quick blurb — e.g., small latency bumps for 0.5% of requests -> acceptable?

Examples of inline comment templates I use:
- blocking: "blocking: behavior relies on implicit ordering of map iteration — can you make ordering explicit or add a test?"
- question: "question: are concurrent writes to `sessionCache` expected here? add a comment explaining safety."
- nit: "nit: remove trailing comma and run `gofmt`"
- suggestion: "suggestion: prefer `sync/atomic` for counter increments to avoid lock in hot path"

When to escalate to a quick sync:
- if 2 or more blocking comments reference different subsystems (e.g., db + runtime), request a 15 min sync to align.
- if changes touch rollout/console or dedicated capacity config, pager the release owner and tag `@release-oncall`.

Common non-blocking acceptance criteria I accept for small PRs:
- tests covering new logic OR a short test plan in PR body + follow-up test ticket assigned.
- no new global locks in hot loops (or proof showing negligible impact).
- documented default behavior in README or docstring.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Would a staged linter catching `TODO: remove after migration` help speed reviews? (ask infra-automation)
- How to measure cognitive load of long review threads? Could try counting reply depth in a week for a random sample.
- Might enable a bot that auto-attaches the Quick-review checklist when PR > 200 LOC.

Small mental reminders before approving:
- check for accidental debug logs ("fmt.Println" / `console.log`).
- ensure feature flag gating for behavior that can be rolled back without code changes.
- note if PR touches `private-deploy` config -> needs security review.

Draft PR comment template (one-liner + checklist):
"Looks good overall. Left a couple of nits and one blocking question about concurrent safety — if that's addressed, I'm happy to approve. Quick checklist: Summary, Size, Tests, Perf risk, DB migration, Rollback plan, Owner."

End-of-note TODOs (actually actionable):
- [ ] convert this checklist into a GitHub PR template (tasked to self).
- [ ] file PERF-PL-1 harness issue and link to PR above.
- [ ] prototype `sequence_length_stats` extraction on a branch and measure latency impact (local spike test).

Slack refs & breadcrumbs:
- thread: #serving-runtime ops discussion 2024-11-12 about KV eviction (search: "kv eviction tradeoffs")
- convo with Maya about perf testing (msg ts 1700001234)

End.

(If I come back later, add quick scoreboard: "last used: 2025-03-04 for PR #4123 review")
